# Cubic mask coverage controls

Six original shapes authored by `tools/svg_cubic_coverage_fixture.py`: symmetric,
asymmetric, fractional, shallow, backtracking and degenerate cubics. Every shape
uses a white rectangular luminance mask so the native raster exposes path alpha
without bitmap resampling. There is no corpus artwork or external dependency in
the fixture. The DOCX contains the usual full, cropped, grouped and shape-fill
instances generated by `canvas_svg_fixture.py`.

The reference application captured the first inline instance read-only. `capture.emf` is
the original range capture; `native.emf` is its nested SVG metafile. The six
PNG files are extracted native mask rasters, not browser-generated expectations.
`metafile-reference.json` binds their hashes, dimensions and transforms.

`native-coverage-reference.json` records native GDI+ flattening at tolerances
0.25, 0.1, 0.01 and 0.001, plus decoded native alpha for dependency-free unit
comparisons. `tools/record_svg_cubic_coverage.py` derives that alpha directly from
the hash-checked PNGs and verifies native half-offset coverage against the reference application.
All six native path captures agree exactly. Nonzero winding with half-open edge
crossings on the tolerance-0.25 native vertices, sampled at x+k/8 and y+j/4,
also agrees exactly with all six native rasters.

These are reference controls, **not a portable flattening implementation**.
Even the collinear degenerate cubic has eight native curve segments at tolerance
0.25. Distance from the endpoint chord alone cannot explain native subdivision.
No renderer changes or full corpus-document fidelity claims follow from these tests.

Local validation: seven reference tests pass. The control opens as one editable
page on port 5173 without runtime errors. No-edit package preservation, insertion,
unrelated-part preservation, exact undo and edited reopening pass. The source and
three browser exports pass all 40 applicable XML schema checks. These workflow
checks do not assert that the current browser's cubic rasterization matches the reference application.

Reproduction:

1. Run `python tools/svg_cubic_coverage_fixture.py`.
2. Capture with `tools/capture-svg-group-raster.ps1`, then extract using
   `tools/record_svg_mask_kernel.py`.
3. Extract `word/media/vector.svg` from the DOCX to a scratch file. Run
   `tools/diagnose-svg-cubic-path.ps1` with width 120, height 80 and each path
   index 0 through 5, using `<captures>/<index>` for each output folder.
4. Run `python tools/record_svg_cubic_coverage.py <captures>
   tests/fixtures/svg-cubic-coverage`.
5. Run `npx vitest run tests/svg-cubic-coverage.test.js`.
